stories.body: Donald Trump, Xi Jinping and Vladimir Putin plan to meet during next week’s Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation summit in Shenzhen, according to the White House. Nuclear arms control and the Iran war are expected on the agenda, while a senior US official said Ukraine would not be discussed. The meeting follows the February expiry of New START, the last treaty limiting US and Russian strategic nuclear arsenals; Trump wants a replacement that includes China. US officials have played down expectations of an agreement, describing the talks as the beginning of a conversation. Neither Moscow nor Beijing had confirmed the trilateral meeting in the supplied reports.
stories.headline: Trump, Xi and Putin plan first three-way summit in China

stories.body: Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent has publicly blamed Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick’s department for delays in restricting Megaspeed, a Singapore-based Nvidia customer reportedly investigated over suspected chip smuggling into China. Bessent said several agencies had supported adding the company to the export blacklist for months, but Commerce controlled the decision. The dispute follows Jensen Huang’s departure as Nvidia chief executive after reports of an affair with a former Megaspeed executive suspected of being a Chinese spy; chief financial officer Colette Kress has taken over temporarily. Lutnick and Huang are due to face congressional questioning next month, with lawmakers seeking answers about export controls and what administration officials knew.
stories.headline: Nvidia scandal brings public clash over US chip-export controls

stories.body: Turkey and Qatar signed a mutual defence agreement on Friday, pledging a unified response to an attack on either country, according to a joint statement by their leaders. The pact follows the Mecca Joint Defence Agreement signed by Turkey, Pakistan and Saudi Arabia in August. The announcement comes amid continuing regional conflict, including fighting in Yemen that is displacing civilians.
stories.headline: Turkey and Qatar sign mutual defence pact

stories.body: International Criminal Court judges have ordered prosecutors to halt investigations into alleged crimes by US personnel and the Islamic State affiliate in Afghanistan, concentrating instead on Taliban conduct since 2021. The ruling cites major difficulties investigating and obtaining evidence; prosecutors said they have already appealed. The US-related inquiry had been deprioritised since 2021. The decision comes amid US sanctions against current and former court staff, although the report does not establish that those measures caused the ruling.
stories.headline: ICC judges halt Afghanistan inquiries into US troops and Islamic State affiliate

stories.body: US authorities lifted a nationwide ground stop on Friday after a telecommunications outage halted thousands of aircraft for more than four hours, leaving widespread delays. Transportation Secretary Sean Duffy blamed old hardware and said US airspace had reopened. Officials ruled out a cyberattack and a broader Microsoft outage, while investigators continued working to establish the cause.
stories.headline: Flights resume after nationwide ground stop lasting more than four hours

stories.body: The United States has lost its measles-elimination status following a resurgence that began with a major outbreak in West Texas in January 2025. Sustained outbreaks subsequently occurred in Utah, Arizona and other states, reversing a landmark public health achievement.
stories.headline: US loses measles-elimination status after sustained outbreaks

stories.body: The Supreme Court has agreed to review a Trump administration policy blocking asylum seekers at the border. The case adds to the immigration disputes the justices will consider in the coming months.
stories.headline: Supreme Court agrees to review Trump’s border asylum restrictions

stories.body: A building collapse in Brooklyn killed eight people and prompted investigations into building safety and code enforcement. Residents had felt shaking for weeks before the collapse, raising questions about whether warning signs received an adequate response.
stories.headline: Brooklyn building collapse kills eight after residents reported weeks of shaking

stories.body: The government has dismissed Renfe president Álvaro Fernández Heredia and appointed Inmaculada Gutiérrez, previously responsible for the operator’s international projects, as his replacement. State lawyer and former Renfe secretary-general Joaquim Hortalà will lead infrastructure manager Adif following Luis Pedro Marco de la Peña’s resignation. The appointments come after the Urda rail accident, which killed 69 people and led to Transport Minister Óscar Puente’s departure, and a week of disruption linked to the drivers’ dispute. Carlos Cuerpo, who is overseeing transport until a new government takes office, has chosen senior officials with technical and administrative backgrounds.
stories.headline: Government replaces Renfe and Adif leaders amid rail crisis

stories.body: Spain’s cybercrime prosecutors have filed a criminal complaint against TikTok’s Spanish subsidiary, asking a Madrid court to investigate possible offences involving the distribution of child sexual abuse material. They have requested immediate removal of the identified content and confidentiality for the proceedings. The complaint follows an investigation by Maldita.es, which reported finding 1,183 explicit items from more than 200 accounts, viewed nearly 48 million times during 35 days of monitoring. Prosecutors said they reviewed evidence submitted by the outlet before taking the matter to court; the investigation will seek to establish the facts and identify those responsible.
stories.headline: Prosecutors file complaint against TikTok over child sexual abuse material

stories.body: Pedro Sánchez and Alberto Núñez Feijóo will hold a televised head-to-head debate on Thursday, November 19, ahead of the November 29 general election. Television Academy president María Casado will moderate the encounter, covering housing, the economy and taxation, social policy and public services, corruption and democratic reform, and migration and foreign policy. Feijóo will open and Sánchez will close following a draw. A separate four-candidate debate has also been agreed, but its date remains unsettled; the head-to-head’s broadcast time had not yet been announced.
stories.headline: Sánchez and Feijóo confirm November 19 election debate

stories.body: Vox wants to review Spanish citizenship granted to more than 300,000 people of Moroccan origin over the past decade. Its election programme promises to examine fraudulent grants of nationality, while party sources told El País they consider all naturalisations of Moroccan citizens fraudulent because Spain generally requires renunciation of prior nationality and Moroccan nationality cannot be renounced. That is the party’s argument; the supplied report does not establish that these citizenship grants were unlawful.
stories.headline: Vox seeks review of citizenship granted to 300,000 Spaniards of Moroccan origin

stories.body: Renfe and drivers’ representatives have agreed to restore previous shifts, timetables and starting stations from Sunday, November 15, aiming to ease a week of Rodalies cancellations and delays. After earlier agreements broke down, drivers had been required to begin work at Barcelona Sants regardless of where their trains were located, leaving some unable to reach early departures. Disruption may continue on Saturday while rosters are rearranged. The agreement does not resolve the wider dispute over working conditions and safety: strikes remain scheduled for November 17 and 23, and further negotiations are planned.
stories.headline: Rodalies drivers’ shift agreement takes effect Sunday, but strikes remain planned

stories.body: The Council of Ministers has approved an expansion of Catalunya’s judiciary, with the main reports identifying 94 new judicial posts and 47 prosecutor posts. Barcelona province will receive 60 of the judicial positions, with criminal, employment and violence-against-women cases among the priorities. The prosecutor allocation would raise staffing from 472 to 519. Reports differ on some judicial totals and implementation dates, with posts expected during 2027 and 2028; one count includes an additional previously created but unfunded position. Legal professionals caution that filling the posts will also require larger recruitment intakes.
stories.headline: Catalunya approved for 94 additional judicial posts and 47 prosecutors

stories.body: Barcelona’s discrimination observatory recorded 284 incidents involving Catalan use in 2025, up from 192 in 2024, an increase of 47.9%. Language became the second most frequently recorded grounds for discrimination, behind racism and xenophobia, among 1,265 situations documented overall. Cases included people unable to obtain services in Catalan at restaurants, healthcare facilities and public offices. Public administration became the leading recorded source of discrimination across categories. City officials cautioned that rising totals also reflect better detection and reporting, so the figures alone do not measure changes in the underlying prevalence of discrimination.
stories.headline: Recorded discrimination over Catalan use rises 48% in Barcelona

stories.body: Barcelona has initially approved a €25.2 million redevelopment beside the future La Sagrera green corridor, including 71 protected homes, additional temporary accommodation and the restoration and expansion of the historic Fàbrica del Plom. The former foundry will house a neighbourhood centre and the Ateneu del Clot. The plan also covers street improvements around Verneda, Escultors Claperós and Concili de Trento, along with the compulsory purchase and demolition of six properties. The work is expected to take four years, with housing construction and management potentially involving the city, another public administration or private partners.
stories.headline: Barcelona gives initial approval to €25.2 million housing and public-space plan
